overview: White meets the Benko with 4.e4, taking the centre rather than accepting the pawn. Black can respond 4...bxc4 5.Bxc4 or 4...cxd5 or 4...Nxe4 tricks, so the play is double-edged and the exact line depends on Black. Strong players rarely meet the Benko this way.

black_ideas.idea: Counter in the centre with ...Nxe4 tricks

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after bxc4 and Bxc4

character.notes: Mixed; the tactics depend on the move order.

gambit.notes: Material level at the root, no pawn offered.

character.reason: Black has options so the line can turn tactical or stay calm.

gambit.reason: Material is level at the root and no pawn has been taken.

structure.reason: The centre is open to different structures.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever choose 4.e4 against the Benko.

level.reason: The ideas are not heavy on theory.

plans.reason: White gains a big pawn centre.
